hard_failures: Item 6 falsely claims that zero-sum least-squares residuals force roughly half the points above and half below the line, and that seven of eight points above could not occur. Zero residual sum balances signed magnitudes, not counts.
incorrect_or_ambiguous_items: Item 6 asks students to justify a false general expectation about the count of residual signs.
errors: The item 6 worked explanation makes an invalid inference from residuals summing to zero.
critical_observations: Independently recomputed all predictions, residuals, r-squared, means, extrapolations, and plotted-point counts.
The observed data happen to split four and four, but that example does not validate the stated general least-squares rule.
artifact_findings: Exactly ten readable worksheet problems were visually confirmed despite the machine problem-count warning.
Machine verification checks the observed fraction but does not test the false explanatory generalization.
rationale: Most regression computations are correct, but item 6 teaches a substantive false property of least-squares residuals, so the strict mathematical-correctness gate fails.
